title: Filmmaker Christopher Nolan describes the challenges of creating "The Odyssey": "It should be hard"
facts: Filmmaker Christopher Nolan directed and wrote the feature film 'The Odyssey'.
Christopher Nolan's film 'The Odyssey' was filmed across six different countries.
'The Odyssey' generated more than $260 million at the worldwide box office over its opening weekend.
The cast of 'The Odyssey' includes actors Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, and Tom Holland.
'The Odyssey' is the first commercial feature film shot entirely using IMAX cameras.
Christopher Nolan stated that IMAX film reels run out of film in slightly under three minutes.
Matt Damon stated in an interview that 'The Odyssey' was the hardest movie he had ever done.
Film scenes for 'The Odyssey' were filmed on location on mountain summits.
Christopher Nolan opted to film actors on real boats in ocean waves rather than using green screen technology.
Christopher Nolan stated that he aspired since his teenage years to shoot a Hollywood feature entirely on IMAX.
Christopher Nolan explained that IMAX cameras fill the viewer's peripheral vision on the largest screens.
Christopher Nolan discussed the production of 'The Odyssey' in an interview with CBS Mornings co-host Gayle King.
Christopher Nolan cited filmmakers George Lucas and Steven Spielberg as major childhood influences.
Christopher Nolan stated that he still experiences nervousness when releasing new films despite his past success.
Christopher Nolan stated that a film is not complete until the audience experiences and interprets it.
